races.name: Racing Welfare Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
British EBF Novice Stakes

runners_data.name: Majestic Jude
runners_data.note: William Haggas-trained two-year-old with a natural hold-up style whose sole outing produced a fifth over this exact trip on Good ground — the redistribution to midfield reflects a field where rear berths are over-subscribed, so expect him to race slightly closer than ideal rather than at his true comfort zone.|

runners_data.name: Moheebb
runners_data.note: John Butler's charge finished sixth on debut over 7f on Good ground and returns with 24 days rest; a genuine hold-up type facing a race where the tempo may not be strong enough to set up the sustained late run his profile demands.|

runners_data.name: Nidal
runners_data.note: Stuart Williams runner was beaten eight lengths on his sole start over 7f on Good ground and carries a notable finishing fade flag — Pierre-Louis Jamin takes the ride but the combination of weak form and a tendency to stop in the home straight makes him a significant risk.|

runners_data.name: On Target
runners_data.note: George Scott's gelding represents the one confirmed pace angle in this field and, racing in a prominent style, faces no rival who will genuinely test him for the lead; STYLE_FIT tag acknowledged — his chance is tempered if the race develops in a way that doesn't reward front-running, but in this shape he is squarely in the box seat.|

runners_data.name: Al Jabbar
runners_data.note: Charlie Appleby's debutant carries the lightly-raced flag and unknown going profile, but the Godolphin operation debuts juveniles in peak condition and Billy Loughnane in the saddle adds a strong jockey angle; entirely unknown style means he could land anywhere in the race order.|

runners_data.name: Astabuen
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's first-time-out runner is equally unexposed with unknown going and style profile, though the trainer's 14-day strike rate of 4/42 is modest; George Downing rides and the horse arrives as a blank canvas — both a risk and an opportunity.|

races.paceDynamic: On Target is the sole confirmed pace-setter in this six-runner field and, with no rival willing to press for the lead, shapes to bowl along at a sustainable, controlled tempo on Good to Firm ground over Newmarket's July Course seven furlongs. That uncontested lead will compress sectionals and make this a test of class and finish rather than stamina, favouring horses that can sit handy and quicken from a position of comfort. The field holds more hold-up types than the rear of the race can naturally accommodate — Majestic Jude, despite being a genuine hold-up operator, has been redistributed to midfield on the map, meaning the true rearward group is thinner than it appears and closers will need to find sustained late momentum without the benefit of a truly fast early gallop to chase. The tactical verdict is clear: a prominent or handy racing profile is best served here, with the debutants Al Jabbar and Astabuen carrying the biggest unknown but potentially arriving fresh and unexposed into an ideal tactical scenario.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: On Target Controls, Stays
scenarios.trigger: If On Target dictates an uncontested, even tempo and his rivals fail to quicken past him in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: On Target rolls to the front unchallenged, sets a rhythm that suits his stamina profile, and the lack of any genuine pace pressure means his lead holds longer than rivals expect; handy types who track him are best placed to pounce but may simply not have the firepower to get by.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Debutant Lands Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If one of the unexposed debutants — Al Jabbar or Astabuen — shows significantly superior raw ability and sweeps past On Target inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: With unknown styles and fresh legs, either debutant could slot in a handy position and produce a turn of foot that outclasses these rivals; Appleby's Al Jabbar in particular carries the firepower of a powerhouse yard that regularly debuts well-prepped juveniles.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Grab Late Spoils
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely brisk enough to set up a strong late run and one of the hold-up types finishes best of all.
scenarios.body: Majestic Jude has the profile of a horse who can close from off the pace, but in a race with only one front-runner setting a moderate tempo, there is limited collapse in the early fractions to exploit; this scenario requires the race to develop faster than expected.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Collapses, Nidal Bounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace evaporates entirely and the field concertinas in the straight, producing a muddling finish where any of the back-markers can land a blow.
scenarios.body: Nidal has a fade warning attached and Moheebb has modest recent form, so this scenario relies on the race deteriorating into a sprint that suits neither; only a complete collapse of normal race shape makes this live.

watchPoints.text: On Target — watch whether George Wood elects to go hard or easy in front; if he is allowed to bowl along unchallenged, the race could be decided by the halfway point as no rival has the early pace to close the gap.|

Al Jabbar — Billy Loughnane's positioning from the gate will be critical; if Appleby's debutant is placed handily in the first few strides it immediately becomes the most dangerous horse in the race given the yard's juvenile debut record.|

Majestic Jude — watch for Harry Davies attempting to position closer than the horse's natural style dictates; if he is shuffled back to a true hold-up position in a race with a single moderate pace-setter, the task becomes very difficult.|

Nidal — the finishing fade flag is worth monitoring in running; if he is travelling well at the two-furlong pole but then visibly weakens, it confirms the flag and rules him out of similar races until the style concern is addressed.|
Astabuen — an unknown first-time starter for Ed Walker whose pre-race market move, if any, will be the only meaningful intelligence available before the off given zero form to analyse.|

races.name: Racing TV Fillies' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Elara May
runners_data.note: Won last time in good-to-firm-adjacent conditions and has strong placed form at 6f in good going; races prominently and is ideally positioned to track a hot pace before producing her effort in the final furlong — Hector Crouch is a capable pilot in these handicaps.

runners_data.name: Powdering
runners_data.note: Michael Herrington's yard is 4/13 over the last 14 days and this hold-up specialist is at her best in strongly-run 6f races where she can pick up the pieces; her last two runs include a win and a third at this trip on similar ground, and the pace shape here is tailor-made.

runners_data.name: Zighy
runners_data.note: George Boughey's three-year-old has won twice on standard turf and is a genuine front-runner who will force the issue from flag fall under Billy Loughnane; the concern is that she faces three other pace rivals fighting for the same lead, which may cost her the controlled race she needs — her best form came when allowed to dominate.

runners_data.name: Shallow
runners_data.note: Wears a visor and tends to race from hold-up, but her recent record shows inconsistency, including a 19th on this course; she has placed in quicker ground at 6f but needs significant early pace to deliver late, which this race should provide — the headgear adds a slight unknown.

runners_data.name: Angel Shared
runners_data.note: Steph Hollinshead's five-year-old front-runner has three wins from 15 starts on good or similar going but recent form reads 5-3-0-6-4-9, suggesting she is coming to the end of a tough campaign; she will force the pace but has shown vulnerability when pressured throughout.

runners_data.name: Bright Summer
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's three-year-old is stepping back from 7f to 6f and has never previously raced at this shorter trip; she has been racing prominently but her five-run form cycle shows declining returns, and the drop in trip adds genuine uncertainty about her stamina versus speed balance.

runners_data.name: Adalida
runners_data.note: Stuart Williams' three-year-old is a front-runner in outstanding recent form — wins in two of her last three — and races over a trip shorter than her recent 5f-6f blend, where she has been devastating on good ground; she is the most in-form pace horse in the race and the biggest danger if she gets a clean early break.

runners_data.name: Seeing Stars
runners_data.note: William Knight's three-year-old wears a hood and races prominently, with a string of placed efforts at 6f-7f in good going; only 10 days since last run is worth monitoring, but she has handled quick turnarounds before and her consistency makes her a legitimate each-way profile if the pace is hot.

races.paceDynamic: Four confirmed front-runners — Zighy, Angel Shared, Bright Summer, and Adalida — will immediately contest early positions over this straight Newmarket 6f, with Billy Loughnane on Zighy and Dougie Costello on Angel Shared both experienced enough to push hard from the gates. This guarantees a strong, pressured gallop from the outset, burning energy through the first three furlongs and stretching the field into a strung-out line by halfway. The hold-up horses Powdering and Shallow, plus prominent types Elara May and Seeing Stars, will be tracking a pace that works directly in their favour, as the front-runners will be fighting for position and burning fuel before the rise into the final furlong. This race shape strongly favours closers and late-running prominent types who can sit off the pace war and produce a sustained finish once the front-runners begin to tie up — Powdering, Shallow, and Elara May are the profiles most architecturally suited to what this pace scenario creates.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace War, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the four front-runners burn each other out inside three furlongs, leaving the field for hold-up and prominent types to sweep through
scenarios.body: Zighy, Angel Shared, Bright Summer, and Adalida create a genuine pace war that sees the leaders visibly weakening approaching the final furlong, opening a clear lane for late-movers; Powdering and Elara May, sitting just off the carnage, are best placed to capitalise on their superior stamina reserves at this trip.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Pacesetter Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Zighy or Adalida gains a clean break and establishes a comfortable margin while rivals waste energy fighting each other
scenarios.body: With one front-runner controlling the tempo rather than a full-scale battle, the race settles into a structured gallop that suits a horse capable of leading without overextending; Adalida's strong recent form — two wins from last three — and her course-going profile give her the profile to hold on if she secures a clean passage in front.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is hot enough to cook the leaders but not extreme enough for deep closers to make up ground from the back
scenarios.body: Elara May, prominent and travelling economically just off the pace, is ideally positioned to slide through on the inner as the front-runners crack; Seeing Stars, who has placed repeatedly in similar company, could also benefit from this middle-ground pace scenario where tracking positions prove optimal.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Shock Closer From Back
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses entirely and turn-of-foot becomes decisive rather than stamina
scenarios.body: Shallow has placed repeatedly in quick-ground 6f handicaps but needs things to fall right from the rear, and a total pace collapse is the only shape that brings her genuinely into the race late; Powdering, while better suited in Scenario A, also carries some residual probability here given her strong recent record on this going.

watchPoints.text: Four front-runners — Zighy, Angel Shared, Bright Summer, and Adalida — will all break forward simultaneously; watch the first furlong closely for bumping, position-fighting, and potential interference that could compromise any of their chances before the race truly begins.

Adalida's recent form surge (two wins from three) makes her the most dangerous pace horse in the race, and if she breaks cleanly and Dougie Costello allows Angel Shared to go forward rather than fight, Adalida could find a cheap lead and prove very hard to catch.

Powdering is 35 days off the track for a trainer in sharp form (4/13 over 14 days); if Michael Herrington has her spot-on for this race, Dylan Hogan has the tactical sense to position her for maximum effect off this pace.

Bright Summer drops from 7f to 6f for the first time in her career — watch her early pace and whether she settles naturally or over-races, as this trip switch is a genuine unknown that could either sharpen her or expose her.

Shallow's visor has not consistently unlocked improvement and her course form includes a distant 19th here; she needs everything to go right from the back, and any traffic issues in a strung-out 8-runner field could end her chance before the finish line comes into view.

races.name: Racing TV Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Liberate
runners_data.note: Hold-up type whose recent form reads poorly (0-9-0-5-5) and whose best similar-ground effort was a win over 13f, suggesting the 1m2f trip may actually be sharp enough to catch her; George Wood rides for a yard with a modest 1/11 recent strike rate and 24 days since last run is an uncomplicated prep.

runners_data.name: Fanciulla Del West
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner here, returning after 50 days for Ed Walker (4/42 recently), with three placings from five starts at similar going and an encouraging 2-2 record at 1m2f on good ground; George Downing takes the ride and the uncontested lead is the defining asset for her chances.

runners_data.name: Emma's Letter
runners_data.note: Billy Loughnane partners a filly who genuinely prefers to come from off the pace, and her form figure of 1 in her last five — a win over 10f on good ground — is the standout performance in this field; the tongue-tie is fitted and Ed Dunlop's 1/17 recent record tempers enthusiasm slightly, but the form profile is live if the pace is genuine.

runners_data.name: Miss Guinevere
runners_data.note: Her natural style is to race held up, and the thin nature of her form (9-5-4 in last three, all at shorter distances) gives limited basis for confidence stepping up in trip; mapped to midfield here because the field's rear is already occupied, and the [STYLE_FIT] flag rightly discounts her chance in a shape that does not require her position — Charlie Fellowes has had three winners from thirteen recently but 64 days off is a flag.

runners_data.name: Port Darwin
runners_data.note: A prominent racer with two wins from fifteen at similar going and back-to-back wins at 1m and 1m1f on good ground earlier in the season; Callum Shepherd rode both victories and the return from just 16 days rest for Charlie Johnston's in-form yard (5/35) suggests this horse is ready to go close from an ideal tactical position tracking the leader.

races.paceDynamic: Fanciulla Del West is the sole confirmed front-runner in this five-runner field and, with no genuine rival to press her, she will dictate from the front at whatever tempo suits Ed Walker's filly over this 1m2f trip on Good to Firm ground at Newmarket's July course. Port Darwin is a prominent type who will likely sit close to the pace in second, ensuring at least some company for the leader, but without a true pace rival to force a genuine gallop the fractions are likely to be controlled and modest through the early and middle stages. Hold-up horses Liberate and Emma's Letter will be doing their running from the rear, and the compressed, unhurried pace profile makes it harder for them to generate the necessary momentum off a slow early tempo. This race shape strongly favours the front-running and prominent profiles — horses positioned on or near the pace will be hardest to peg back in a likely steadily-run contest on a flat, unrelenting track where those at the head of affairs can conserve and then quicken.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Controls, Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Fanciulla Del West dictates a comfortable, uncontested pace and kicks clear in the straight.
scenarios.body: Fanciulla Del West sets a measured tempo with Port Darwin tracking, and without genuine pace pressure she arrives at the two-furlong pole full of running; her Good-to-Firm form (two placings from five at similar ground) and Ed Walker's 4/42 recent form suggest a well-prepared filly capable of seeing it out.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Port Darwin tracks the pace closely and proves strongest when Fanciulla Del West's advantage narrows in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Port Darwin brings winning form over 10f on good ground and Charlie Johnston's yard has a solid 5/35 recent record; Callum Shepherd can time the challenge from second to deliver a decisive late thrust past a tiring leader.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closer Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or the early gallop is faster than expected, producing a truly-run race that opens up the closing stretch for rear-ward runners.
scenarios.body: Emma's Letter showed a win and three placings in eleven similar-going runs and Billy Loughnane is an astute judge of pace; if the fractions are genuine she has the profile to pick up ground through the final two furlongs, though this scenario depends on conditions rarely delivered in a five-runner field.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Blows Open, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Fanciulla Del West is inconvenienced at the start or burns energy uncharacteristically, scrambling the expected shape entirely.
scenarios.body: With only five runners and a clearly mapped hierarchy this scenario is the least likely, but any incident leaves Miss Guinevere — a genuine hold-up type forced further forward than ideal — poorly placed; Port Darwin and Emma's Letter, both with winning recent form, would become the chief beneficiaries of any positional chaos.

watchPoints.text: Watch Fanciulla Del West's early tempo — if George Downing allows her to coast in front at a very slow pace over the first half-mile, the hold-up horses Liberate and Emma's Letter will be denied the run-in they need to generate momentum.

Port Darwin's positioning in the first furlong is critical; if he fails to sit directly behind Fanciulla Del West and allows a gap to open, he risks gifting the leader an unassailable advantage before the race becomes a contest.

Emma's Letter's chance is almost entirely conditioned on the pace being honest — in a five-runner race at Newmarket where the sole front-runner is uncontested, monitor whether the sectionals through the first half-mile suggest a genuinely-run race or a steadily-run dawdle.

Miss Guinevere's 64-day layoff combined with an upward step in distance and the style redistribution note all converge; watch for signs of greenness or lack of match fitness in the early stages as she tries to find a position that isn't naturally hers.

Going is officially Good to Firm for the 3:45 per the race-day report — confirm no significant watering has altered the strip, as all five runners carry similar-going tags of OK but the surface plays fastest through the July straight where front-runners historically hold a strong advantage.

races.name: End Of Summer Season Handicap Stakes (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Rizal
runners_data.note: Won twice over 10-12f on Good recently and arrives as the only front-runner in this four-horse field, giving jockey Billy Loughnane a priceless positional advantage; the STYLE_FIT tag notes he may be racing slightly out of his most comfortable role, but with no pressure coming, that concern is minimal over this distance.

runners_data.name: Patrol
runners_data.note: Consistent form over 12f including a third and two seconds, and trainer Dylan Cunha has a fair 14-day strike rate (4/22); though mapped to midfield here, Patrol's true preference is to race from the rear of the field, a position only fully rewarded if Rizal sets a genuinely strong gallop — the redistribution reflects a crowded hold-up division, not a change of style.

runners_data.name: Parisian Scholar
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's charge carries strong recent form (two consecutive 12f wins on Good) and has Callum Shepherd in the saddle; a natural hold-up runner over a distance he has clearly mastered, the concern is whether a slow pace from Rizal will blunt the closing kick — but of the hold-up trio, Parisian Scholar's course-relevant form makes him the most compelling late challenger.

runners_data.name: Zurna
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 3yo who won over 12f on Good last time and is stepping up in class in handicap company; 43 days off is worth noting but connections have a modest recent trainer strike rate (1/3 in 14 days), and Dylan Hogan takes the ride — the ability to track closer than the other hold-up horses could prove decisive if this develops into a sprint finish.

races.paceDynamic: Rizal is the sole confirmed front-runner in a four-horse field and, with no rival likely to seriously contest the lead, faces a straightforward task in setting whatever tempo suits from the front at 1m4f on Good to Firm ground at Newmarket's July course. The three hold-up horses — Patrol, Parisian Scholar, and Zurna — will track from varying positions behind, with Patrol redistributed to midfield on the map despite being a true hold-up type, simply because the rear of the field is crowded with closers. The race shape will almost certainly see Rizal bowling along at a controlled, unhurried gallop, which on this flat, fair track risks turning the contest into a sprint test from 2f out, favouring those with tactical speed over deep staying ability. This race shape firmly favours Rizal's front-running profile and any hold-up horse with a sharp enough turn of foot to pounce on a steady-pace leader — pure grinding stayers are at a disadvantage if the fractions are modest.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Rizal Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Rizal leads at a comfortable, unhurried tempo and is never seriously pressured through the race.
scenarios.body: Rizal dictates the fractions from the front, dictating a moderate pace that keeps the hold-up horses' closing runs in check over 1m4f on fair ground; with no rival able to match his front-running role, he simply picks up his own gallop entering the straight and holds on. Horses that stay handy and can quicken from a close-up position are best placed to challenge, but the leader's ability to control the race makes him the primary beneficiary.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Trio Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If Rizal's solo lead creates a falsely slow pace and the closers find gears in the straight to overhaul him.
scenarios.body: A strongly stamina-oriented 1m4f trip at Good to Firm can still produce a late flourish if the pace is so modest that the hold-up horses arrive with a meaningful advantage in energy reserves entering the final furlong; Parisian Scholar, with two recent wins over 12f on Good, and Zurna, who won last time over 12f Good, both have the form to finish powerfully. The field as a whole is hold-up heavy, meaning the closing burst could be densely contested inside the final 2f.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Zurna Tracks And Quickens
scenarios.trigger: If Zurna, lightly raced and improving, sits close enough to Rizal to pounce at the top of the straight.
scenarios.body: Zurna's recent win over 12f on Good and a solid second at 10f suggest a horse still on the upgrade, and a small field of four allows a clean passage to challenge Rizal entering the home straight; if Rizal's gallop is honest, Zurna's freshness (43 days off) could prove an edge. This scenario benefits horses who can time their challenge from just behind the leader rather than deep hold-up positions.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Patrol Delivers From Rear
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong and Patrol, a true hold-up type, lands a late challenge from the back.
scenarios.body: Patrol's redistribution to midfield on the map masks his natural preference to race from the rear, and only a truly honest pace from Rizal would create the stamina test needed for a deep hold-up run to succeed over 1m4f; even then, Patrol's recent form (6,3,4,2,2) shows consistency without a convincing win. This scenario is the least likely given Rizal's expected control and Patrol's out-of-role positioning.

watchPoints.text: Rizal's jockey Billy Loughnane controls the tempo entirely — watch whether he allows a truly sedate gallop that compresses the finish into a 2f dash, which would significantly reduce the hold-up trio's chances.

Parisian Scholar has won twice consecutively over 12f on Good ground but hold-up horses need a honest pace to deliver — if the fractions are slow, his closing run may not materialise fully despite superior form.
Zurna is 43 days off the track and steps into handicap company for the first time; monitor market moves to judge whether connections believe the horse is cherry-ripe or slightly underdone.

With only four runners, the field is dominated by hold-up horses (three of four), meaning a genuine late finish between Parisian Scholar, Zurna, and Patrol is possible even if Rizal makes most — watch for traffic implications inside the final 2f when all three closers converge.

Patrol's true hold-up style is masked by his midfield map position — if Rizal sets only a crawl, Patrol's deepest finishing run is the least likely to succeed, and punters should not read the map position as a natural prominent racing style.

races.name: See You On The Rowley Mile Fillies' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Rogue Citation
runners_data.note: Trainer Bethell in good 14-day form (9/25), ran 14 days ago and won over this exact trip and going last time; a naturally prominent racer who will want to press forward but faces real congestion with four others wanting the same ground, making a clean passage the key variable.

runners_data.name: Splash
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist who won last time over course and trip on good ground, fitting this race surface ideally; the 37-day break is a minor query but Dean Ivory runners fresh rarely need a run, and if the pace is fierce she is the one most likely to arrive late with a sustained finish.

runners_data.name: Miss Gallant
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner whose only two career runs produced a win and a fourth, both at the 7f trip, and she carries headgear (hood) that suggests Botti wants her controlled from the front; off 47 days but her profile screams pace-setter and she is one of the two most likely horses to actually dictate throughout.

runners_data.name: Too Too Divine
runners_data.note: Won over 6f on good ground and placed over this trip but her going figures on good are modest (2/4); James Fanshawe's mare wants to race prominently and will be competitive for early position, though she may get shuffled wider with multiple rivals pushing forward.

runners_data.name: Allegrino
runners_data.note: The other confirmed front-runner, with a strong recent record including two wins at 7f and consistent placing in similar company; Andrew Balding's runner is fit from a 20-day break with good form on this surface (3/8 sim-going) and will contest the lead directly with Miss Gallant — which of the two blinks first shapes the entire race.

runners_data.name: Ironist
runners_data.note: A genuine prominent racer by style, but the field congestion around that position means she is unlikely to get her natural berth; George Margarson's four-year-old has a poor sim-going record (0W2P in 8 runs on good) and racing out of role compounds an already difficult assignment — treat her chance in any scenario requiring that position with caution.

runners_data.name: Hilltop
runners_data.note: Billy Loughnane partners the top-weighted five-year-old who has solid placing form over this course and trip on good ground (1W2P in 6 sim-going runs); prominent racer who is likely to secure that position ahead of Ironist in the competitive early stages, and her course familiarity is a genuine asset.

runners_data.name: Bami
runners_data.note: Won last time out after a break and Tom Dascombe has a live runner here with solid good-ground form over 7f (1W1P in 5 sim-going runs); naturally prominent and likely to slot into the first group behind the front two given her recent sharpness, making her well placed to exploit a pace battle.

runners_data.name: Ghisa
runners_data.note: True hold-up type (hood worn) with three of her last five runs producing placed finishes on similar ground, but all three of her good-ground runs have seen her finish 7th or 8th; Charlie Fellowes' filly needs a strong gallop and an unobstructed run to make late ground count, and her record on this surface is the honest concern.

races.paceDynamic: Miss Gallant and Allegrino are the two confirmed front-runners and will fight for the early lead from the gates, creating a genuinely contested gallop across the opening two furlongs of this 7f Rowley Mile trip. With four of nine runners wanting prominent positions — Rogue Citation, Too Too Divine, Hilltop, and Bami all pressing forward — there will be significant congestion on the heels of the leaders between the 3f and 2f poles, creating real traffic danger for those trapped on the wrong side. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural position; Miss Gallant and Allegrino are most likely to actually lead, with Hilltop and Bami best placed to slot into the first wave of prominent spots, while Rogue Citation and Ironist face the most likely squeeze. An honest, competitive gallop from an early stage suits a mid-to-prominent racer who settles just off the heat and has the cruising speed to pick off the tiring leaders in the final furlong — making the prominent-but-not-lead profile the clear tactical beneficiary on this flat, straight track.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Miss Gallant and Allegrino fight for the lead and set a genuine pace that softens the front two, allowing a prominent racer tracking just behind to swoop
scenarios.body: The early battle between the two front-runners burns them out sufficiently that a horse settled in the first group off the pace hits the rising ground in the final furlong with most left to give; on this straight, flat Rowley Mile course, there is nowhere to hide and the horse with the best late stride off a sound gallop wins

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two front-runners — most likely Miss Gallant — dictates without excessive pressure and controls the tempo to deny closers a strong enough gallop to reel her in
scenarios.body: A controlled but honest gallop that denies the hold-up runners a true target could see the leader simply find too good a rhythm to be caught on a flat, undemanding track; Miss Gallant's recent winning form and headgear application both support this profile

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Fliers Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is blistering and the front-runners crack catastrophically in the final two furlongs, creating a vacuum that genuine closers can exploit
scenarios.body: Splash and Ghisa are the truest hold-up types here and both carry recent course and going form over 7f, but this scenario requires everything to go right positionally on a straight track where getting blocked is a genuine danger; the pace must be truly severe and the hold-up pair must find clear daylight in the closing stages

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Traffic, Blanket Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent logjam causes interference two furlongs out and the race unravels into a muddling, stop-start affair that scrambles the form lines
scenarios.body: Sustained bunching between the 3f and 2f markers knocks runners out of their rhythm and produces a compressed, unpredictable finish where any horse still in a good position at the two-pole benefits from the lottery; horses like Too Too Divine and Rogue Citation, who have shown tactical versatility, could capitalise on disorganisation

watchPoints.text: Miss Gallant and Allegrino will go head-to-head for the lead from the off — watch which one breaks fastest from the stalls, as the one who controls the front end without a fight has a markedly better chance of lasting home.

Monitor Ironist and Rogue Citation at the two-furlong marker — with four horses contesting the prominent positions, these two are the ones most likely to get squeezed or checked in the critical section where runners fan across the track.

Hilltop is the top weight at 140lbs carrying significantly more than her rivals — watch whether Billy Loughnane can get her to settle just off the pace rather than being dragged into an early battle, as her weight becomes a greater burden the more energy she expends early.

Splash is the freshest of the true hold-up horses at 37 days since her last run — watch her position rounding the final two furlongs; if she is travelling strongly in fifth or sixth with a clear passage, Robert Havlin is likely to make an early move to avoid the closing traffic.

The going report confirms Good to Firm for this race despite the stated Good going — a faster surface than expected will shorten strides and potentially compress the finish, which benefits the horse who travels with the most ease in the final three furlongs rather than relying purely on late acceleration.
